title: Verified Facts Must Lead Vietnam’s Dog Trade Reform
excerpt: A stolen companion, illegal shipment, or health warning demands proof—not rumor. Public safety needs transparent enforcement and complete abolition by 2030.
body_html:
When rabies symptoms appear, survival is virtually impossible. That is why every possible exposure demands immediate wound washing with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes, followed by urgent medical assessment and post-exposure prophylaxis when indicated. World Health Organization guidance makes this clear.

Myths cannot replace proof

Claims about stolen pets, poison bait, illegal transport, or uninspected slaughter require named cases, dates, locations, and official records. Those details are not available here. No responsible campaign should invent a raid, conviction, victim, shipment, or outbreak to intensify emotion.

Biosecurity has no room for evasion

Rabies spreads when infected saliva enters through bites, scratches, broken skin, or mucous membranes. Handling sick animals, bite attacks, and uninspected slaughter can create risk. Properly cooked meat is not an established rabies transmission route. Household exposure incidents and commercial supply-chain failures must be investigated as separate dimensions of broken biosecurity, not falsely joined as one event.

Vietnamese communities deserve accountable reform

Families deserve protection from animal theft. Pet owners deserve transparent investigations. Communities deserve quarantine enforcement, traceable transport, humane veterinary controls, and accurate public-health reporting. Lawful activity, regulatory breaches, and criminal theft must remain clearly distinguished.

SDE calls for complete abolition of the dog meat trade by 2030. Sign the national petition to add your name to that public demand, then follow campaign updates as it reaches decision-makers: sign the national petition.

telegram_message:
Rabies turns preventable exposure into near-certain death once symptoms begin.

• WHO guidance: wash any possible exposure with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes.
• Seek urgent medical care. Post-exposure prophylaxis can include vaccination and, when indicated, rabies immunoglobulin or approved monoclonal antibodies.
• Verified reporting must name dates, locations, agencies, court records, or health alerts. Rumor cannot prove stolen-pet networks, poison bait, illegal transport, or contaminated meat.
• Household exposure and commercial trade-chain failures require separate investigation.
• Vietnamese families deserve protection from theft, unsafe handling, and enforcement gaps.

SDE demands complete abolition of dog meat trade by 2030. Sign petition: https://c.org/nLZTZdVNdJ

Vietnamese families, pet owners, veterinarians, and local leaders can demand stronger quarantine controls, traceable transport, humane enforcement, and transparent investigations.
